components: a tall left upright joined to a low crossbar
an inner upright and broad right bowl
a lower hook joined to the inner upright's tail, with a short exit
strokeOrder: start at the lower left and climb the tall upright
without lifting, retrace down the same upright
without lifting, carry the low crossbar to the right, on round the bowl's foot, and up its right side
without lifting, come back left over the top of the bowl into the inner upright
without lifting, descend the inner upright into the stem below the baseline
without lifting, run round the lower hook to its tip and back round it into the short exit — and only now lift
strokeOrderNote: one stroke — the manual numbers six movements; native writers draw them without lifting, and this ductus follows them in order on the print face, carrying the low crossbar round the bowl's foot and running round the lower hook to its tip and back; cited to Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I, Frame 7, ழ

strokeOrderSource.citation: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 7, ழ (University of Texas at Austin), p. 193
strokeOrderSource.variation: Appendix I Frame 7 numbers six movements: 1–3 form the left body and bar, 4–5 the inner upright and broad right bowl, and 6 the lower hook. Native writers draw them as one continuous stroke, and this ductus follows them in order without lifting. The bundled Noto Sans Tamil print face simplifies the source's looped left body and high bar into a retraced upright with a low crossbar that runs straight into the bowl's foot, so movement 3 carries on round the foot and up the bowl's right side, movement 4 comes back left over the top into the inner upright, and movement 5 descends it into the stem below the baseline. The face joins the hook to that stem only at the hook's far end, so movement 6 runs round the hook to its tip and comes back round it into the short tail. In HP Labs India's online Tamil handwriting data (the LipiTk 4.0 Tamil isolated-character recognizer, trained on hpl-tamil-iso-char), 97% of the 182 stored prototypes of ழ are a single pen-down stroke. Tamil handwriting varies by school; this is one attested order.

notes: The famously Tamil retroflex approximant, often transliterated ḻ. Frame 7's six numbered movements are one continuous stroke: up and back down the left upright, along the low crossbar and round the broad right bowl, down the inner upright, and round the lower hook.
